title: Coherent reflexive sheaves on regular schemes of dimension at most two are finite locally free
statement: Let $X$ be a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme] of topological Krull dimension at most two [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $F^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Call $F$ reflexive if the evaluation morphism $F\to F^{\vee\vee}$, sending a local section $s$ to the functional $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(s)$, is an isomorphism. Then $F$ is reflexive if and only if $F$ is finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf].

proof.text: By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $X$ is locally Noetherian and $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a Noetherian regular local ring for every $x\in X$. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $\dim R$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of generalizations of $x$. Taking closures gives chains of irreducible closed subsets of $X$, so [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim X\le2$ give $d=\dim R\in\{0,1,2\}$. No connectedness or integrality of $X$ is being assumed.

The structure module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (on an affine chart it is the associated module of the coordinate ring, with generator $1$), hence is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent] makes $F^\vee$ coherent as well. A coherent module is locally finitely presented: choose a finite set of local generators, then finite local generators for the kernel, which is of finite type by the definition [pqf-def-coherent]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-source-stalk] separately to $F$ and $F^\vee$ gives finite presentations of $M=F_x$ and $N=(F^\vee)_x$ over $R$; in particular both are finite.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation] first to $(F,\mathcal O_X)$ and then to $(F^\vee,\mathcal O_X)$, using step 2. This identifies $N$ with $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ and $(F^{\vee\vee})_x$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)=M^{**}$. The evaluation formula in [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-evaluation] shows that the stalk of the sheaf evaluation is precisely $m\mapsto(\lambda\mapsto\lambda(m))$: a local functional applied to a section has germ equal to its stalk map applied to the section germ. Consequently if $F$ is reflexive, this algebraic evaluation $M\to M^{**}$ is an isomorphism for every $x$.

proof.text: If $F$ is finite locally free, take the trivializing open cover and finite ranks of [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Apply [lem-sf-locally-free-sheaf-evaluation-biduality] on the Zariski site with $R=\mathcal O_X$ and $M=F$; an open cover has the covering-sieve property in that statement. Its evaluation $\delta_F$ is the evaluation in the item, since both send $s$ to the local functional $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(s)$. The cited lemma therefore gives its invertibility, including rank zero and varying ranks. This proves the finite-locally-free-to-reflexive implication.

For the converse suppose $F$ is reflexive and fix $x$. If $d=0$, regularity says that the maximal ideal of $R$ has zero generators and is therefore zero. A nonzero element of this local ring is outside its maximal ideal, hence a unit; thus $R$ is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free], $M$ is free. It is already finite by step 2, so a basis is finite: a finite generating set uses only finitely many basis vectors and spans $M$, forcing every basis vector to be among them.

If $d=1$, [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] makes $R$ a discrete valuation ring, in particular a domain. The module $M$ is torsion free: if $0\ne a\in R$ and $am=0$, then for every $\lambda\in M^*$, $a\lambda(m)=\lambda(am)=0$, hence $\lambda(m)=0$. Therefore evaluation sends $m$ to zero, and its injectivity from step 3 gives $m=0$. Now [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] applies to the finite module $M$ from step 2 and gives that it is finite free.

If $d=2$, choose two generators $a,b$ of the maximal ideal, as allowed by regularity. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], they form an $R$-regular sequence in the maximal ideal, so [def-weil-pbc-depth] gives $\operatorname{depth}R\ge2$. Apply [new-local-dual-depth-two] to the finite module $N=(F^\vee)_x$ from step 2. It yields $\operatorname{depth}\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)\ge2$. By step 3 and reflexivity this module is isomorphic to $M$; linear isomorphisms preserve multiplication, quotients by each parameter and their injectivity, hence preserve regular sequences and depth. If $M=0$, it is free of rank zero. Otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives $\operatorname{depth}M\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}M\le\dim R=2$; the second inequality holds because every chain of primes in the support is a chain in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Hence $\operatorname{depth}M=2$, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-mcm-free] makes the finite module $M$ finite free. The zero-module case was separated because its depth is infinity, not two.

proof.text: Steps 5--7 give a finite free stalk $F_x$ at every point. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian and $F$ is coherent, [lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free] applies and proves that $F$ is finite locally free. Together with step 4 this proves the equivalence. If $X$ is empty, the stalk condition is vacuous and the same criterion applies, equivalently the empty trivializing cover suffices.
